newsitem.title: USA: Countrywide August loan production dips.
newsitem.headline: Countrywide August loan production dips.

text.p: Countrywide Credit Industries Inc said Thursday it funded $3.0 billion of mortgage loans in August, down from $3.2 billion in August 1995.
Loans in process total $4.3 billion, an 18 percent decline from $5.2 billion a year earlier, it said.
For the six months ended August 31, total loan production was $20 billion, a 29 percent increase over the same period in 1995.
The servicing portfolio rose to $149 billion at August 31, 18 percent higher than $126 billion a year earlier. It had a weighted average coupon of 7.8 percent, the same as last year.
Countrywide said its fixed-rate loan production amounted to $2.1 billion in August, or 67 percent of total production, versus $2.4 billion, or 76 percent of total production, last year.
Purchase mortgage activity was $2.4 billion in August, up from $2.2 billion in August 1995. Refinances were 20 percent of total fundings compared to 32 percent in August 1995.
The company funded $42 million of home equity loans in August, up from $19 million in August 1995. Sub-prime loan funding activity was $63 million, up from $1 million in August 1995.
